summary.headline: Som Distilleries Q1 FY27 hit by Madhya Pradesh suspension: consolidated EBITDA INR15.2 crore on INR268.8 crore total income; FY27 revenue guidance cut to INR1,000-1,100 crore.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was described by management as an extremely difficult quarter, driven by the operational and regulatory disruption in Madhya Pradesh, where the Bhopal brewery remains suspended. Consolidated volume was 45.79 lakh cases, total income INR268.8 crore and EBITDA INR15.2 crore. Karnataka (cases up about 30%) and Odisha (up about 40%) recovered, and the UP brewery (about 10 million cases capacity) began commercial production around June 9, 2026. Gross debt rose only INR10 crore QoQ, with gross D/E moving from 0.3x to 0.31x, and operating cash generation was about INR28 crore. FY27 revenue guidance was lowered to INR1,000-1,100 crore from the earlier INR1,400-1,500 crore.

financial_highlights.value: 45 lakh cases, about 98.9% of total volume and 93% of revenue

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue lost from MP closure in Q1
Raw material and packaging cost increase (cans, malt, bottles)

segments.name: Madhya Pradesh (Bhopal brewery)
segments.commentary: Operations suspended for about six months; licence restoration is pending in courts and with authorities. Fixed cost run-rate about INR6-7 crore per quarter including interest, salaries and power, of which about INR5 crore is employee cost (standalone). Finished goods stock about INR25 crore, with roughly one month of shelf life left per management.

segments.name: Karnataka (Hassan)
segments.commentary: Cases sold up about 30% in Q1; plant utilisation about 60%. Sunny Beaches reported as performing well here.

segments.name: Odisha
segments.commentary: Cases sold up about 40% in Q1; plant utilisation about 70%.

segments.name: Uttar Pradesh brewery
segments.commentary: Commercial production started around June 9, 2026; about 10 million cases annual beer capacity; about INR300 crore spent on Phase 1 with no pending capex per management. Utilisation not yet meaningful given lean season. Management says peak utilisation is 3-4 years away.

segments.name: IMFL (Mahavat)
segments.commentary: Realisation up about 3% YoY to INR1,047 per case. Mahavat launched in Bhopal, Delhi and UP; supply resumption from Bhopal is a stated focus.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance cut to INR1,000-1,100 crore from earlier INR1,400-1,500 crore; margin guidance deferred to next call.
Management says the MP licence issue should be resolved in the current month, but it is not in management's control and is sub judice.
Andhra Pradesh direct sales expected to start by first week of September 2026, pending export permissions from Karnataka.
Plan to step into the Indian single malt category before end of FY27 (in-house developed).
Phase 2 (distillery) at UP: permissions applied; firmer execution view in three to four months.
capex_capacity: UP brewery Phase 1: about INR300 crore spent, no pending capex; commercial production from around June 9, 2026.
UP brewery capacity about 10 million cases per year; management says peak utilisation is 3-4 years away.
Hassan utilisation about 60%; Odisha about 70%; Bhopal (MP) suspended.
Company has four beer capacities; MP is one of them and is currently suspended.
Management did not give a firm Phase 2 capex figure; said more clarity in three to four months.
demand_pricing: Karnataka and Odisha recovery offsets MP loss; management says market share retained or growing where brands were available, except MP and partly Delhi.
Raw material and packaging costs up about 7.5-8% YoY; cans rely on a single supplier (Ball Corporation) for the industry.
Excise duty paid rose because more volume was sold in Karnataka and Odisha, where excise is paid before dispatch unlike MP.

Beer portfolio: Hunter, Black Fort, Power Cool, Sunny Beaches, Legend (management listed five; analyst cited Woodpecker as well). Management says the multi-brand approach targets different price segments.
Receivables: most sales are to government wholesalers in the states where the company operates, and management sees no material receivable risk.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue was lost from the MP closure in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR250-260 crore of revenue was lost.

qa_highlights.question: Will Bhopal (MP) be restored, and what was the FY27 outlook if it is not?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the matter is in courts and with authorities and is sub judice; it is hopeful of resolution this month. It declined to discuss a plan B or give numbers for a no-approval scenario, and reiterated FY27 revenue of INR1,000-1,100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Could Karnataka or other plants supply Bhopal to lift utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said importing from Odisha or UP to MP would be uneconomic because of MP's very high import fees, potentially leading to a loss.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Andhra Pradesh entry go live?
qa_highlights.answer: Excise and corporation permissions were delayed until end-July; export permissions from Karnataka are pending, and brands are expected in AP by first week of September.

qa_highlights.question: Should the company use contract manufacturing in states with overcapacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it compares local contract brewing against importing and chooses whichever is better on margin and quality, and that capacity is planned over five to 10 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Hassan plant not converted into a 100% subsidiary like UP?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will evaluate and revert soon, with no commitment.

risks_watch: MP licence restoration timing: court and authority dependent; management has already missed its earlier 15-day restart timeline.
Consumer share loss in MP after a prolonged stock-out; management says recovery will be slow in long-closed markets.
FY27 revenue guidance cut to INR1,000-1,100 crore; margins not guided.
Cost pressure: packaging and raw material inflation of about 7.5-8%; single-supplier dependency for cans.
UP brewery utilisation in off-season and competition from new entrants such as UBL in UP.
Related-party/structure questions (SOM Distilleries Private Limited, Hassan 78% holding) were not answered on the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Karnataka, Odisha and UP, but defensive and evasive on MP, deferring to courts and declining to discuss a no-approval scenario or plan B. Management also declined to discuss the private group entity and gave limited detail on margins.
key_quotes: Let me begin by acknowledging that Q1 was an extremely difficult quarter for the company.
The facility adds approximately 10 million cases of annual beer capacity, giving us a significant new manufacturing and marketing -- market access platform.
We generated close to INR28 crores of cash from operations during the quarter.
I think I will stay with my guidance of INR1,000 crores of revenue.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.why: UP brewery with about 10 million cases/yr capacity began commercial production around June 9, 2026 after about INR300 crore Phase 1 spend, though management says peak utilisation is 3-4 years away.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: by end of FY27 (Andhra Pradesh go-live first week of Septemb
rows.why: Management plans to enter the Indian single malt category before end of FY27 (in-house developed) and Andhra Pradesh direct sales are expected in the first week of September 2026, pending Karnataka export permissions.

rows.label: Bhopal (MP) brewery licence restoration
rows.why: Management hopes to resolve it this month, but it is in courts and with authorities; the Bhopal brewery has been suspended for about six months and the fixed cost run-rate is INR6-7 crore per quarter, with about INR25 crore of finished goods stock nearing end of shelf life.

rows.label: Packaging and raw material inflation
